title: 1.1 Write `test/journeys/journey-sources.test.ts` (scenario "The journey sources read as the rules say"; it reads the two journey files with `readFileSync`, so it is red until they exist) first. Then write `test/journeys/m7-tools.test.ts` (test `carol registers three servers and alice dry-runs through all three adapters`, scenario "Carol registers three servers and alice dry-runs through all three adapters"; `before` runs `startE2eStack({ port: 0, controlPort: 0 })` and asserts the handles `durable`, `egress`, `tools`, `tool-servers` and `mcp`), implementing requirement "The tools journey works against the real engine". It is green on arrival (the stack and the earlier units are its proof), so the harness may raise a `pre_satisfied` question for it, as in `add-web-dry-runs` task 5.1; the source test is the criterion that is red first. In the same task (the addendum writes the browser journey in a task that also adds Node tests) write `e2e/test_m7_tools.py` (test `test_carol_sets_up_three_servers_and_alice_dry_runs`, marked `@pytest.mark.milestone("M7")`, scenario "Carol sets up three tool servers and alice's dry run reads, runs and stubs"; it follows `e2e/test_m6_grants.py`), implementing requirement "The M7 journey proves tool registration, review and a dry run in a browser". A red step cannot run `e2e/`: its criterion stays out of `criteria_ids` and the verifier checks it; `criteria_ids` holds the source scenario and the Node journey scenario

notes:
C-eba5ac9e is covered only by the browser journey, which I did not run. Its locators come from the existing e2e files and `test-plan-browser.md`.

`GET /api/v1/policy-decisions?limit=200` returns 500 INTERNAL. The handler in `src/api/audit-routes.ts` asks `listPolicyDecisions` for limit+1 = 201 rows, and `src/pdp/decisions-query.ts` rejects anything above 200. The test plan says limit=200, so I used limit=100. This is an engine defect for a later change, not something I fixed. No assertion depends on the limit value.

Two details in the Node journey are my own reading of the test plan. For `log_note` it checks the effect, the two flags and the hints, but not the call text, which the plan elides as "…". For `headers.authorization` it expects the literal "[credential]", which is what the fake proxy records.

The journey files contain the throwaway values `e2e-crm-key` and `e2e-ledger-key` as the plan names them. They are not token-shaped, and the Node test asserts that no recorded request or decision holds them.
